Apologies in advance to anyone reading these and seeing yet another tomlinas post on bees.

We're not fucked. We're not even in mild amounts of trouble. Au contraire, bees are doing better than they ever have before and the number of beehives is at a record high. What these clickbait articles either don't tell you, or dance around (as this one does), is that wild bees are in decline due to removal of their habitat and surging numbers of domestic bees. They'd like you to think it's the big mean old neonicotinoids which no study has been able to link conclusively to bee damage, or that all the bees are dying and OMG save the bees!

In reality, bee demand is driven almost entirely by honey demand. Honey demand is surging. Honey is getting more expensive because there is more demand than there is supply, even though supply is growing every year -- it just can't keep up with demand growth.

A nice little side effect? An abundance of pollinators, which is decreasing the cost of pollination for farmers all over (well, the ones that depend on pollinators, anyway)

Now, the conservation of wild species is an interesting topic in its own right and we should probably care about the wild bees. However, the farming industry is not only at zero risk from this wild bee decline, it is actually benefiting from the rapid growth of domestic bees.
